headline: Memory-efficient algorithms for partial order alignment and variation graph construction
label: Genome Graph Construction And Alignment
summary: Recent preprints and papers report linear-space POA alignment, lower-memory colored k-mer indexing, and faster pangenome graph construction.
synthesis: The common thread is reducing the memory and runtime costs of operations on sequence graphs and related indexes. linearPOA recasts partial order alignment as a parallel, divide-and-conquer procedure with linear space complexity, reporting up to 102.74x lower memory than abPOA. LCPAN applies locally consistent parsing to pangenome variation graph construction, reporting over 12x speed and 13x lower memory than vg. Kaminari addresses a related engineering problem in a different data structure, a colored k-mer index that combines minimizers with integer compression to support approximate document queries, reporting lower memory and faster queries than the comparators named in its full text. The novelty across these items lies in algorithmic reformulations, specifically linear-space alignment and parsing-based graph construction. Reported comparative figures are tied to specific baselines in each item and should be interpreted within that context.
